name: template-manifest
body: Template schema as data: a template's schema — one-line `description`, `fields` (name, type, required, default, limits, variants, formats/default format, description), `sections` (name, accepted section templates, min/max) and `body` rule — is declared in its `template.yaml`, not in Go code. The `sections:` schema is exactly the one slides use and applies unchanged to a section template: a section template that declares `sections:` gives itself child sections, so composition nests (template-composition). A container section template typically declares `body: {mode: disallowed}` and holds only its declared child sections. A template's kind (slide|section) comes from its directory (`templates/slides/` or `templates/sections/`); `usage:` is not a `template.yaml` key, and its presence is a templates error. The schema vocabulary is exactly the existing one (field-types, body-rules, template-composition, template-variants, number-date-formats). The template's example is `example.md`, parsed and validated like a deck slide (no hand-written structured example); a container template's example may contain nested instances and is validated recursively (nested-section-validation). AC: no template schema lives in Go source; a `template.yaml` containing `usage:` is rejected with a path-qualified templates error; a section template declaring `sections:` loads and its example with nested instances validates.
